findings.description: The "spec `suggestion` is always null" guard is tied to the finding's final area, not to the reviewer that wrote it. The new §6 rule ("a defect the code alone proves stays `correctness` or `security`"), and dedup's "merge into one finding", can move a `review-spec` finding into `correctness` or `security` while keeping its suggestion. Nothing in the schema, the validator or the poster removes it, so a suggestion written after reading attacker-authored issue text can still be posted as a committable suggestion.
findings.body:
The spec-suggestion guard is tied to the final area, so issue text can still reach a committable suggestion.

§8 now nulls "a `spec` finding's `suggestion`" ([SKILL.md#L154](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/10f1e85717975657bc17bb3200b307ff56d49637/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L154-L154)). This same delta also adds a §6 rule that takes a `review-spec` finding out of `spec` whenever the code alone proves the defect ([SKILL.md#L123](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/10f1e85717975657bc17bb3200b307ff56d49637/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L123-L123)). Dedup (L122) merges findings without saying whose `suggestion` survives.

The spec reviewer is still told it may return a `suggestion` (L102), and `review-spec.md` never forbids one. After that, nothing enforces the rule:
- In `tools/review/src/review-metrics.schemas.ts`, `suggestion` is a plain nullable string with no link to `area`, and the record doesn't say which reviewer wrote a finding.
- `review-validator.md` never looks at suggestions.
- `tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts` L74-78 renders any non-null suggestion as a committable ```` ```suggestion ```` block when the anchor wasn't moved.

**How it's reached:** someone files an issue on this public repo, and a PR says `closes #N`. `review-spec` reads the attacker's issue body. It returns a real defect the code alone proves, carrying a crafted `suggestion`. §6 files the finding as `correctness`, and the opus validator confirms the defect without checking the replacement code. The poster then publishes it as a one-click commit.

Fix: tie the rule to the reviewer that wrote the suggestion, not the area the finding ends up in. Also say it at the source in `review-spec.md` ("your `suggestion` is always `null`").
findings.suggestion: - **`suggestion` is committable code, so it must be exactly right.** Only for a small self-contained fix that resolves the finding entirely. The poster renders it as an inert fence rather than a committable block whenever it had to relocate the anchor, since applying it there would rewrite a line the finding never mentioned. A `suggestion` that `review-spec` wrote is always `null`, whatever area the finding consolidates under (§6), merges included: its fix would rest on issue text, which the validator can only check against that same text (why `--fix` skips it).

findings.description: §3's rewritten parenthetical is hard to parse: "which you pass on as its bare number, the only form `gh` takes under CI (§5), since the shell reads an unquoted `#12` as a comment" nests a parenthesis inside a comma-spliced aside, and the `since` clause reads as the reason a bare number is the only form, when that reason is the §5 lock. Suggested: "which you pass on as its bare number (the only form `gh` takes under CI, §5; an unquoted `#12` is a shell comment)".

§6's new clause ("a defect the code alone proves stays `correctness` or `security`") is followed by the old sentence "Otherwise a real defect is `correctness` or `security`", which now repeats it. Drop the old sentence, or reword it as the default case ("Any other real defect...").
